title: Many Lines of Output
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how several print() calls make several lines of output.
learn: Each print() usually makes one new line
Stack print() calls to build a longer message
The order of your print() calls is the order of the output
idea: One print() shows one line. If you want three lines, you use three print() calls. Python still runs from top to bottom, so the first print() shows up first in the output, then the next, then the next. The output always matches the order you wrote the code in.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Room 12 to Room 8 and press Run. Only that middle line of the output should change.

practice.text: Finish the school schedule so it prints three class names on three lines. Fill in the blanks.
practice.hint: Math is already on the first line. Each empty print() needs a different subject name in quotes.
practice.starterTip: Fill the two blank print() lines, for example print("Science") and print("Art").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if there are three print() calls that each show a non-empty class name or subject.

practice.text: Make a four line shopping list. Keep the title and fill in the three blank item lines.
practice.hint: Keep print("Shopping list") as line one. Each of the three blank print() lines needs one item in quotes.
practice.starterTip: Try print("Apples"), print("Milk"), and print("Bread") on the three blank lines.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if there are four print() calls with non-empty text (title plus three items).

quiz.question: How do you print three separate lines?

options.text: Use one print() with no quotes
Use three print() calls, one after another
Python only allows one print per program

quiz.correct: Right, stack print() calls and each one makes another line.
quiz.wrong: Comments do not print anything. You need multiple print() calls.

quiz.question: If print("A") is above print("B"), what appears first?

options.text: Both on the same line as AB

quiz.correct: Yes, it goes top to bottom, so A prints before B.
quiz.wrong: The output follows the same top to bottom order as the code, so check which one comes first.

quiz.question: What happens if you delete one print() from a four-line poster program?

options.text: You usually get three lines of output

quiz.correct: Right, fewer print() calls usually means fewer lines of output.
quiz.wrong: Every print() you keep still runs. The one you deleted is just gone.
